absent: Numeric values and bit layouts for trap markers, flag bits, feature masks, control registers, command codes, CPU class identifiers and notifier codes.
Memory layouts for register frames, thread and task state, probe descriptors, return instances and virtual 8086 images.
Allocator limits, address space constants and shadow stack update contract.
Signal delivery, fault injection and interrupt subscription primitives.
Debug interception table format and trace handling policy beyond the shown checks.
Linker placement and boot handoff expectations for the physical startup entry.
Concurrency rules for probe hooks and per thread virtual state beyond the shown bitmap guard.

findings.text: Provides a predicate that reports whether the calling thread left the expected uprobe trap state, returning affirmative when the recorded trap number differs from the uprobe marker.

Defines completion of out of line execution where the saved trap number is reinstated, an optional architecture post handler may run and on failure the recorded fault address becomes current with restart converted to success and trap signalling suppressed, a pending single step indication produces a trap signal, and the step flag is cleared when it was not present on entry.

Serves as a die chain observer that ignores traps without user context or from kernel mode, claims breakpoint events handled when a pre single step probe fires and debug events handled when a post single step probe fires, otherwise leaves the event unclaimed.

Abort of out of line execution preserves the option to run an abort hook, then reinstates the saved trap number and recorded fault address and clears the step flag when that flag was introduced locally.
Offers an emulation shortcut where absence of an emulate hook means no skip, and a successful emulation combined with a set step flag raises a trap signal to the current thread.

Exposes a return address replacement service that reads the user stack slot sized for the current address width, leaves an already replaced slot untouched, installs the supplied trampoline address, synchronizes shadow stack state, and reports the prior address on success.
Partial or failed user stack update during return address replacement is treated as corruption with a forced fault signal and a failure marker returned instead of an address.

Liveness of a return probe instance is judged from the current stack pointer against the recorded call site value, using a strict comparison immediately after call entry and an inclusive comparison elsewhere.

Reports whether a probed instruction sits at function entry by requiring an active uprobe task and then accepting either a frame setup byte or, in 64 bit mode, a branch terminator pattern at the saved instruction start.

Allocation of the execute out of line area temporarily advertises compatibility status when the address size flag is set so that the generic allocator applies the intended limit, then clears that temporary status before returning the chosen address.

Performs an early processor acceptance check that preserves caller flags, probes for identification support, records vendor lineage from identification words, clears an execute disable inhibit on selected Intel families through a control register only when the bit was set, enforces required capability masks from base and extended leaves, retries vector support enablement once on AMD lineage, and signals success with zero and failure with nonzero while restoring flags.
Safe flag mask fact is 0xDD5 and return flag mask fact is 0xDFF for virtual 8086 flag handling.
Virtual 8086 interrupt registration name fact is vm86irq and the permitted signal set fact allows no signal plus user and input related signals.
Interrupt reservation state consists of sixteen entries each pairing an owning thread with a signal number, plus a global pending bitmap and a dedicated spin lock guarding that bitmap.
Pending interrupt bitmap updates execute under an interrupt saving spin guard that atomically tests and clears the requested bit and reenables the corresponding line only when the bit had been set.

Legacy entry accepts a user virtual 8086 image and forwards it in non extended mode, while the multiplexed entry routes interrupt management requests to a dedicated handler, acknowledges an install probe with success, and forwards enter requests in extended mode.

Virtual 8086 entry establishes a one shot per thread session. It requires permission to map low address space, rejects reentry once a session is active and rejects the obsolete screen bitmap option, captures user registers and redirection state, derives stored virtual flags from user input merged with protected mode heritage plus virtual mode enablement, selects a virtual flag mask from declared processor class, preserves kernel stack and segment state while adjusting entry paths, and on success presents the virtual register image as the current trap frame.

Virtual flag access distinguishes full width stored flags from a short view of the same storage, accumulator low byte access addresses the first byte of the saved general register, and log messages carry a module prefix.

Virtual flag updates apply a per thread mask to stored flags and the safe mask to visible flags, and keep the virtual interrupt indicator consistent with the requested interrupt bit. The dedicated set helper only raises that virtual indicator.

Guest stack transfers for fault emulation use byte granular user accesses that adjust the guest pointer per unit and divert to a common failure path when any access faults, with wider values composed from ordered byte operations.

General protection fault handling in virtual mode skips address and operation prefixes, emulates flag push and pop with width sensitivity, dispatches software interrupts with optional debug interception, emulates far return with width sensitivity, and toggles the virtual interrupt state for clear and set operations. Completion may exit for pending virtual interrupts, forced returns, preserved trace handling, or unknown operation, while any guest memory access failure exits as unknown.

Interrupt management restricts bit query and reset to the owning thread, returns the whole pending bitmap on request, allows reservation only to privileged callers with an allowed signal and a valid free line, allows release only to the owning thread, and rejects unknown operations.

Crash metadata collection on 32 bit records indirection and paging mode facts when configured, while on 64 bit it additionally records the physical base, top level table location, paging level indication, image relocation and size, and memory encryption mask.
Provides the physical startup link entry used for the 32 bit boot path.
Stored flag writability depends on declared processor class from none through progressively larger sets covering nested task, privilege level, alignment check and identification capabilities.
